key_insight: NavTrust provides a unified benchmark that systematically corrupts inputs for both Vision‑Language Navigation (VLN) and Object‑Goal Navigation (OGN) to quantify model robustness and trustworthiness, revealing how small real‑world corruptions break otherwise high‑performing agents.
problem_solved: Current embodied navigation evaluations assume nominal inputs and miss real‑world corruptions; NavTrust fills this gap by offering a standardized corruption suite and metrics to evaluate how reliable navigation agents are under realistic perturbations.
method: Design a systematic corruption suite across modalities (vision, language, sensors) with controllable severity levels to simulate real‑world noise and failures.
Define unified robustness/trustworthiness metrics (e.g., performance degradation curves, trust scores) that compare model behavior across VLN and OGN tasks.
Benchmark state‑of‑the‑art navigation models on the corrupted inputs and provide diagnostic analyses of failure modes and sensitivity patterns.
impact: NavTrust gives researchers and practitioners a practical tool to quantify and compare the real‑world reliability of embodied navigation systems, guiding development of more robust, safer agents and informing deployment risk assessments.
visual_elements: Corruption grid: icons showing corruption types (blur, occlusion, noisy language, sensor drop) × severity levels
Robustness curves: line charts showing performance vs. corruption severity for multiple models
Trajectory overlays: example agent paths in clean vs. corrupted conditions highlighting failure points
Model comparison matrix: heatmap of trust scores across VLN and OGN tasks for several baselines
paper_title: NavTrust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness for Embodied Navigation
paper_authors: Huaide Jiang, Yash Chaudhary, Yuping Wang, Zehao Wang, Raghav Sharma
